sources.entry: ANALOG - A minimal analytics tool. Tracks events in a span of 10-30 days. MIT Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: ANALOG is a minimal, self-hosted analytics tool that records named events and shows them over a rolling 10–30 day window.
summary.what_it_does: It stores event counts through a small Node.js API (POST an event name to /api/events) and serves a web dashboard that plots the events for a configurable time range. The database is pluggable: the README lists MongoDB, PostgreSQL, Redis and SQLite (via libsql/Turso or a local file) and selects one with ANALOG_DATABASE_PROVIDER. Access can be protected with a bearer-style token, optionally only for POST requests. A clean-up step removes old data, triggered either on GET requests or by a scheduled function. The README says it is heavily inspired by piratepx.
use_cases: counting custom events over the last 10 to 30 days
deploying a simple analytics page on Render, Koyeb or Vercel
storing analytics in SQLite, Redis, MongoDB or PostgreSQL
how_to_run: Create .env.local with your settings (database provider and connection URL, ports, token).
Run: npm run dev (launches the frontend app and the Node server)
Alternatively, build with the Dockerfile: docker build -t analog-analytics ., then docker run with ANALOG_STATIC_SERVER=true and the database variables set.
notable: Pluggable storage backend chosen by a single environment variable
Dashboard time range configurable from 10 to 30 days
Deployable as a Docker container or to Netlify, Vercel, Render and Koyeb using included config files
Simple REST API: GET returns counts per event, POST records an event name
Optional token protection for the dashboard and for POST requests
caveats: Scheduled clean-up may not work on Netlify or Vercel because of runtime limitations
PostgreSQL should be used with a transaction pooler connection
Several environment variables need the VITE_ prefix and are baked in at build time
The README is a brief setup guide with no stated maturity or maintenance status
